facts.value: 2+2 structure, whereby students spend their first two years studying at UL and their remaining two years at the dual degree partner.
The remaining two years includes a Co-op placement.
Students graduate with a degree from UL, as well as a degree from the partner School.
There are no extra academic fee implications for students as no academic fees are paid to the partner institution and students just pay their normal fee to UL over their four years.

facts.value: The Department of Accounting and Finance is one of four constituent Departments in the Kemmy Business School at the University of Limerick. The Department has responsibility for the disciplines of accounting, finance, risk management and insurance, taxation and corporate social responsibility.
Faculty in the Department of Accounting and Finance have a variety of professional and academic qualifications, experience working in practice and in industry.

This strongly underpins the achievement of excellence and relevance in the teaching of the core disciplines, providing students with knowledge and skills that will guarantee that they are at the cutting edge of a rapidly changing business world, now and into the future.
The department has close links with industry, the professional bodies in accounting, tax and insurance, and the public sector.
Graduates may avail of exemptions in the areas of Accounting, Financial Services, Sustainability and Climate Risk, and Risk Management and Insurance.
The Department of Accounting and Finance is responsible for the delivery of many undergraduate and postgraduate programmes.
Our modules are also core elements on many other, non-Business programmes throughout the University of Limerick.
The Department offers supervision up to doctorate level in its research areas.

The Department of Management and Marketing is one of four departments within the Kemmy Business School and encompasses a teaching and research community across the disciplines of Marketing, Management, Information Management, Communications, Project Management and Entrepreneurship.

The Department makes a strong contribution to the Bachelor of Business Studies Programmes (BBS) undergraduate and graduate programmes of the Kemmy Business School and delivers modules across disciplines to non-business students.
We offer a suite of Postgraduate programmes.
The Department has an active research culture, much of which is conducted in collaboration with a range of industry partners in private and public sectors.

International Human Resource Management, Cross-cultural management, Intercultural issues in management, Marketing and Business Strategy, Customer Value, Marketing Resources and Capabilities, Branding, Services and Relationship Marketing, E-service quality, Interactivity and e-relationship marketing, Consumer Culture Theory, Marketing Leadership theory, Marketing in profit and non-profit sectors, Entrepreneurship Education and Social Entrepreneurship.
Faculty have won prestigious regional and national Excellence in Teaching Awards.
The department holds regular seminars and conferences and contributes to public discourse through expert commentary featured in print, radio and online media.

facts.value: If you are interested in completing an Erasmus+ EU Staff Training mobility, attending a Staff Week organised by one of UL's partner universities may be a good option. Staff Weeks are usually designed to give an overview of the host university's institution and departments, while bringing together teaching and non-teaching staff to share ideas and potentially establish connections for future collaboration.

facts.value: Incoming staff wishing to participate in Erasmus+ Staff Teaching or Training activities must be individually accepted by a staff member in the host department who is responsible for organising the teaching and/or training activities.
Acceptance is dependent on all parties in advance: the participant, the sending institution, and the host department at the University of Limerick.

Agreement for hosting staff members is dependent on agreeing in advance to the contents of the teaching/training plan, the timing of the mobility, and the presence of a signed Erasmus+ inter-institutional agreement (mandatory requirement for Staff Mobility for Teaching).
Potential visiting staff members will need to contact the relevant department in the first instance.
